Write
\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]
For any \(k\le 10000\), write
\[
k=503a+b,\qquad 0\le b<503.
\]
By Lucas’s theorem,
\[
\binom{10000}{k}
=\binom{19\cdot503+443}{a\cdot503+b}
\equiv \binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}\pmod{503}.
\]
Thus this binomial coefficient is \(0\pmod{503}\) whenever \(b>443\).

Since \(503\equiv1\pmod{502}\),
\[
k=503a+b\equiv a+b\pmod{502}.
\]
For potentially nonzero terms, \(0\le a\le19\) and \(0\le b\le443\), so
\[
0\le a+b\le462<502.
\]
Therefore, for \(0\le r\le462\),
\[
S_r\equiv \sum_{a+b=r}\binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}
=\binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}
\]
by Vandermonde’s identity. Because \(462<503\), none of the factorials in \(\binom{462}{r}\) is divisible by \(503\), so
\[
S_r\not\equiv0\pmod{503}
\qquad(0\le r\le462).
\]

For \(463\le r\le501\), there are no potentially nonzero terms with \(a+b=r\), so
\[
S_r\equiv0\pmod{503}.
\]
The number of such indices is
\[
501-463+1=39.
\]

\]

Let \(p=503\), so the residue classes defining \(S_r\) are modulo \(p-1=502\).

First write \(10000\) in base \(503\):
\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]
Similarly, write each \(k\) as
\[
k=503q+s,\qquad 0\le s<503.
\]

By Lucas’s theorem,
\[
\binom{10000}{k}
\equiv \binom{19}{q}\binom{443}{s}\pmod{503}.
\]
Thus this binomial coefficient can be nonzero modulo \(503\) only when
\[
0\le q\le19,\qquad 0\le s\le443.
\]

Because \(503\equiv1\pmod{502}\),
\[
k=503q+s\equiv q+s\pmod{502}.
\]
For the potentially nonzero terms,
\[
0\le q+s\le19+443=462<502.
\]
Therefore, for \(0\le r\le462\),
\[
S_r\equiv
\sum_{q+s=r}\binom{19}{q}\binom{443}{s}
=\binom{462}{r}\pmod{503},
\]
by Vandermonde’s identity.

Since \(462<503\), none of the binomial coefficients
\[
\binom{462}{r},\qquad 0\le r\le462,
\]
is divisible by \(503\).

For \(463\le r\le501\), there are no potentially nonzero terms modulo \(503\), so
\[
S_r\equiv0\pmod{503}.
\]
The number of such \(r\) is
\[

\]

Let \(p=503\), so \(p-1=502\). Work modulo \(503\).

For \(0\le r<502\), define
\[
T_r=\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{503}^{\times}}a^{-r}(1+a)^{10000}.
\]
Expanding,
\[
T_r=\sum_{k=0}^{10000}\binom{10000}{k}
\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{503}^{\times}}a^{k-r}.
\]
For any integer \(t\),
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{503}^{\times}}a^t=
\begin{cases}
502\equiv -1\pmod{503},&502\mid t,\\
0\pmod{503},&502\nmid t.
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore,
\[
T_r\equiv -S_r\pmod{503}.
\]

Now
\[
10000=19\cdot 502+462.
\]
For \(a\ne -1\), Fermat's theorem gives
\[
(1+a)^{10000}=(1+a)^{462}.
\]
This also holds for \(a=-1\), since both sides are \(0\). Hence
\[
T_r=\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{503}^{\times}}a^{-r}(1+a)^{462}.
\]
Expanding again,
\[
T_r=\sum_{j=0}^{462}\binom{462}{j}
\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_{503}^{\times}}a^{j-r}.
\]
Because \(0\le j\le462\) and \(0\le r\le501\), we have \(j\equiv r\pmod{502}\) only when \(j=r\). Thus
\[
T_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
-\binom{462}{r},&0\le r\le462,\\
0,&463\le r\le501.
\end{cases}
\]
Since \(T_r\equiv-S_r\),
\[
S_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r},&0\le r\le462,\\
0,&463\le r\le501.
\end{cases}
\pmod{503}.
\]
For \(0\le r\le462\), \(\binom{462}{r}\not\equiv0\pmod{503}\), because all factorials involved are less than the prime \(503\).

Therefore precisely \(S_{463},S_{464},\ldots,S_{501}\) are divisible by \(503\). Their number is
\[
501-463+1=39.

\[

502\equiv -1\pmod{503},&502\mid t,\\
0\pmod{503},&502\nmid t.
\end{cases}

\[

\]

\[

\[

\[

\]

\[
T_r=\sum_{a\ne0}a^{-r}(1+a)^{462}
=\sum_{j=0}^{462}\binom{462}{j}
\sum_{a\ne0}a^{j-r}.
\]

Because \(0\le j\le462\) and \(0\le r\le501\), the only possible multiple of \(502\) among \(j-r\) is \(0\). Hence

\[
T_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
-\binom{462}{r},&0\le r\le462,\\
0,&463\le r\le501.
\end{cases}
\]

Since \(T_r\equiv-S_r\), we obtain

\[
S_r\equiv
\begin{cases}
\binom{462}{r},&0\le r\le462,\\
0,&463\le r\le501.
\end{cases}
\pmod{503}.
\]

\[
r=463,464,\ldots,501

\[
501-463+1=39.

\[

\[

\[
